title: Add RAG session-router websocket tool-adapter samples and lightweight runner
author: Nora Patel
description: Motivation: provide a compact, production-adjacent example that demonstrates using a WebSocket-based tool adapter to route multi-turn RAG sessions between a lightweight orchestrator and remote tool workers. This PR includes: a minimal session-router sample that preserves per-session KV cache and connector affinity; a WebSocket tool-adapter library (TypeScript) that implements the proposed tool-call protocol used by our browser and edge stubs; an instrumented lightweight runner for local dev that exposes compact telemetry probes and structured output validators; and docs and quickstart content to guide engineers through running the stack locally and on Redwood Private. Highlights: - Focus on session isolation (tenant + session id) and graceful reconnect semantics for unstable networks. - Structured output validator that enforces a simple contract for tool responses and wires into the quickstart e2e smoke check. - Telemetry presets for local dev (span names, sampling hints, and example counters) to make it easy to surface perf regressions without needing full backend instrumentation. The description below is a concise checklist and instructions. Checklist: [x] session-router library + example runner [x] websocket tool-adapter shim [x] README quickstart and troubleshooting guide [x] telemetry preset + smoke CI job [x] unit tests for adapter edge cases Usage notes: the runner exposes a /ws endpoint for agent connections and a separate control HTTP port for starting/stopping synthetic sessions. The README contains a small curl-based smoke scenario and a snippet to connect a browser-based tool worker. Backwards compatibility: the tool protocol is intentionally opt-in; the adapter includes a compatibility shim for our older HTTP-based tool-caller. Related: ENG-1124 (session routing performance), ENG-1199 (tool-call contract spec).
